strategies.name: Put Short Strategy
strategies.risk: Unlimited risk (as stated in the notes).
strategies.structure: Sell an ATM or OTM put; ITM is also mentioned for traders with more directional conviction. The notes prefer OTM for beginners.
strategies.why: Bullish market. The notes describe put selling as a way to trade a positive short-term sentiment.
execution: Sell a put option, generally ATM or OTM.
For a beginner, the notes suggest an OTM put.
Use risk management such as a stop-loss or strategy adjustment.
adjustments: When the sold OTM put becomes ATM as the market moves against the position, do not roll the put down according to the notes.
Sell a call with approximately the same Delta as the put; at ATM this is around 0.50.
The resulting position becomes a short straddle with near-neutral Delta.
If the market consolidates or reverses, the adjusted position can benefit.
triggers: Underlying moves against the sold put.
Example trigger in the notes: Bank Nifty tests the sold-put strike and the put becomes ATM.
mind: Option selling carries significant risk; the notes specifically call for stop-losses or other risk management.
The source example says the adjustment converts the position into a short straddle.

strategies.name: Call Short Strategy
strategies.risk: Unlimited risk (shown in the payoff example).
strategies.structure: Sell a call option instead of buying a put.
strategies.why: Bearish market; the notes particularly mention considering the strategy when implied volatility is a bit high and call premiums are elevated.
execution: The notes use high IV / elevated call premium as an additional consideration.
adjustments: If the index continues to rise, close the extra position after realizing a profit and open a new call position at a higher level.
The purpose described is to collect additional premium and raise the upper breakeven.
triggers: Price moves upward against the short call.
The notes show an adjustment after the market moves beyond the original area.
mind: High IV is specifically mentioned as a consideration.
Risk management is important because the payoff example shows undefined maximum loss.

strategies.name: Bull Put Spread
strategies.structure: Sell a higher-strike put (generally ATM/OTM) and buy a lower-strike put; net credit.
strategies.why: Moderately bullish; best when the underlying is expected to stay constant or rise.
adjustments: Create an additional credit spread on the opposite side.
The Delta of the new credit-spread legs should match the original put-spread Delta.
Use the same strike width on both sides.
This reduces directional risk by moving total Delta toward zero.
The modified payoff resembles a short iron condor.
triggers: Market moves against the bullish put spread / loss needs to be reduced.
mind: The source example says the adjustment reduced maximum loss but also changes the payoff profile.
Keep the strike gap the same on both sides.

strategies.name: Call Debit Spread (Bull Call Spread)
strategies.risk: Low-risk, low-reward according to the notes; net debit.
strategies.structure: Buy a lower-strike call (usually ITM/ATM) and sell a higher-strike call (usually OTM).
strategies.why: Moderately bullish and expecting the price to increase.
adjustments: If price moves against the expected direction, compare the CE buy and CE sell premiums.
Sell another CE with premium approximately equal to the difference between the buy and sell CE premiums, aiming for total short-leg premium equal to or greater than the long-leg premium.
If the market finds support and rebounds, square off the newly created second short position; the notes describe the original call debit spread as restored/modified.
triggers: Price moves against the expected bullish direction.
Potential rebound/support is then considered for removing the additional short.
mind: The source emphasizes protecting capital if the original view fails.

strategies.name: Long Call Calendar Strategy
strategies.risk: Maximum risk is the net debit paid, as described.
strategies.structure: Buy a call at a later expiry and sell a call at an earlier expiry, same strike. Delta-neutral in the notes.
strategies.why: Moderately bullish / gradual appreciation rather than an immediate sharp move.
execution: Sell the nearer-expiry CE at the same strike.
adjustments: Price down: adjust when Delta of an option reaches about 0.30–0.35. Book profit on the near-term short CE and create a new short CE near the current market price.
Price up: adjust when both calls are ITM and Delta is about 0.65–0.70. Close the near-term short CE with loss and sell a CE in the long expiry to create a long-term bull call spread.
When choosing the new long-expiry short strike, aim for MTM close to zero.
Do not make the adjustments more than twice, because increasing strike separation creates Delta imbalance and greater risk in a sudden reversal.
triggers: Upside: both calls ITM and Delta ~0.65–0.70.
mind: Maximum profit is approximate and depends on factors including volatility of the long call.
The notes explicitly limit adjustments to two.

visual.trigger: DOWN: Δ 0.30–0.35  |  UP: both ITM + Δ 0.65–0.70

strategies.name: Bear Call Spread
strategies.structure: Sell a lower-strike call and buy a higher-strike call; net credit.
strategies.why: Moderately bearish / sideways or downward market.
execution: Do not deploy if the reward-to-risk ratio is greater than 1:2, as stated in the notes.
adjustments: If the stock crosses the breakeven, create a put spread in the opposite direction.
Keep the same width between strikes.
The notes state that this can reduce potential loss and additional transactions can reduce maximum loss while increasing possible return.
mind: The source gives a specific reward-to-risk deployment filter: greater than 1:2 means do not deploy.

strategies.name: Bear Put Spread (Put Debit Spread)
strategies.risk: Limited risk, limited reward; net debit.
strategies.structure: Buy a higher-strike put (normally ITM/ATM) and sell a lower-strike put (normally OTM).
strategies.why: Moderately bearish / expecting the underlying to be unchanged or slightly declining in the near future.
adjustments: When the difference between the long and short option Deltas falls from about 0.20 to about 0.10, the notes say it is time to intervene.
Sell another put to obtain extra credit.
Select the put so that its credit is almost equal to the initial debit, bringing overall Delta down toward about 0.20.
The sell-PE price should be almost equal to or greater than the buy-PE price to obtain some credit.
triggers: Delta difference between long and short options shrinks to about 0.10.
mind: The source frames this as a loss-elimination adjustment rather than a new directional entry.

strategies.name: Long Put Calendar Spread
strategies.risk: Net debit; modified downside risk can increase, as noted.
strategies.structure: Buy a longer-term PE and sell a shorter-term PE.
adjustments: Adjustment 1 / price rising: when Delta reaches near 0.20 (or price approaches upper breakeven), book profit on the near-term short PE and open another short PE near the current price where Delta is about 0.40.
Adjustment 2 / price falling: when Delta reaches near 0.70, close the near-term short PE and short a PE in the next expiry, choosing a strike so modified MTM is as close to zero as possible.
triggers: Price approaches upper breakeven / Delta near 0.20.
mind: The notes warn that the modified strategy can increase maximum downside risk and reduce maximum upside risk.

strategies.name: Short Strangle
strategies.risk: Unlimited risk of loss if the index moves erratically outside the range, according to the notes.
strategies.structure: Sell an OTM CE and an OTM PE with the same expiry but different strikes.
strategies.why: Sideways / range-bound market with call writing above and put writing below creating a range.
execution: Sell OTM CE and OTM PE in the same expiry.
Initial short-option Delta is typically 0.20–0.30 on each side.
adjustments: Adjust when the Delta of one short strike roughly doubles.
A conservative alternative is to adjust when a breakeven is breached.
If market rises: take some profit on the sold PE and sell a new PE at a higher strike so total Delta approaches zero.
If market keeps rising, continue moving the PE higher until the short-call strike; the position then becomes a short straddle.
triggers: Conservative trigger: a breakeven is breached.
mind: The notes describe call sellers as a ceiling and put sellers as a floor in the range example.
Adjustment can progressively transform the strategy into a short straddle.

visual.trigger: One side Delta roughly doubles  |  Conservative: BEP breach

strategies.name: Short Straddle
strategies.risk: Undefined maximum loss in the payoff example.
strategies.structure: Sell a CE and PE at the same strike and same expiry.
execution: Initial option Deltas are around 0.50 each, producing near-neutral Delta.
adjustments: Begin adjustment when Delta of either option rises to about 0.75–0.80, or wait until a breakeven is being tested.
If market falls: book some profit from the PE and sell a CE with Delta approximately equal to 0.75.
If market rises: close the profitable PE and sell a new PE at a higher strike.
The notes say the short straddle may be modified only twice; after that, option Deltas can approach one and adjustment costs can hurt the portfolio.
mind: The notes explicitly cap modifications at two.
Extreme adjustments have a cost and can hurt the portfolio.

visual.trigger: One side Delta reaches 0.75–0.80  |  Or BEP test

strategies.name: Short Iron Condor
strategies.risk: Defined/hedged range strategy; payoff in notes shows limited maximum loss.
strategies.structure: Four legs: bull put spread + bear call spread; short put strike below short call strike.
strategies.why: Sideways / stable range. It is described as a hedged variation of the short strangle.
execution: Keep the short put strike below the short call strike.
Overall Delta is intended to be close to zero.
adjustments: Adjust when Delta becomes significantly imbalanced.
The notes give a practical trigger: when the Delta difference between an option combination/spread is twice, modify the iron condor.
Alternatively wait until a breakeven is reached and use steps similar to short-strangle adjustment.
Close the pair of the spread that is making profit when Delta has doubled.
triggers: Significant Delta imbalance / Delta difference doubles.
mind: The source emphasizes monitoring and modification as needed.

visual.trigger: Delta imbalance / spread Delta doubles  |  Or BEP reached

strategies.name: Short Iron Butterfly
strategies.risk: Limited by the long wings in the payoff structure; source shows a defined maximum loss.
strategies.structure: Sell two options at the same central strike and buy two options at different outer strikes; essentially a hedged short straddle.
strategies.why: Range-bound market with little volatility; expects the underlying to remain steady inside a range.
execution: Sell the central CE and PE at the same strike.
Buy the outer call and put as hedges.
adjustments: Modify as soon as Delta starts to deviate; a simpler approach is to wait until a breakeven is violated.
If market turns bullish and tests the upper breakeven, book profit on the put option pair.
The resulting structure is described as an inverted strangle.
The notes say short straddle / short iron butterfly should be modified only twice.
mind: After two modifications the notes advise stopping because Deltas can approach one.
Extreme adjustments can hurt the portfolio.

strategies.name: Double Calendar Spread
strategies.risk: Maximum loss is confined to the net debit in the scenario described.
strategies.structure: Combine a long-call calendar with a long-put calendar; near-term short strangle hedged by longer-term call and put options.
strategies.why: Calm/range-bound situation where volatility is expected to rise soon. The notes say not to establish it when IV is contracting.
execution: The sold near-expiry options can be at the same strikes as the long options, but the notes say same strikes are not essential.
The notes also say a near-expiry option can be selected with premium similar to the sold current option.
adjustments: Start adjustment when Delta changes suddenly; the practical trigger given is Delta difference of ±20–25.
Otherwise monitor the relevant breakeven threshold.
If price rises substantially and touches the upper breakeven and you believe the underlying will rise further, roll up the put pair for more credit.
If price decreases, make the CE pair adjustment described in the notes.
triggers: Expected volatility rise + calm market for initial deployment.
mind: Calendar spreads are positive Vega in the notes and are sensitive to volatility changes.
The notes caution against deployment when IV is decreasing.
Adjustment can increase profit potential but also marginally increase maximum risk.

visual.adjlabel: UP → roll put pair  |  DOWN → CE pair adjustment
